summary.text: Clay Higgins is the U.S. Representative for Louisiana's 3rd Congressional District, an Army veteran and former law enforcement officer who won the seat in a December 2016 runoff in his first race for public office.

He is a core member of the House Freedom Caucus, chairs the Federal Law Enforcement Subcommittee of the House Oversight and Government Reform Committee, and also sits on the House Armed Services Committee.

paragraphs.text: Higgins was born August 24, 1961, in New Orleans, and his family moved to Covington, Louisiana, when he was six.
He graduated from Covington High School and attended Louisiana State University.
He is an Army veteran, and his campaign website says he received his initial police training as a military police officer in the U.S. Army.
Higgins spent much of his career in law enforcement and maintains an active commission and Louisiana State POST certification.

The Advocate described him in 2016 as a reserve deputy for the Lafayette City Marshal's Office and a former captain with the St. Landry Parish Sheriff's Office, and as a viral Crime Stoppers video star who ran as a tough-talking outsider in his first bid for public office.

He finished second in the November 8, 2016 open-seat primary, with 26 percent to Scott Angelle's 29 percent, then defeated Angelle, a fellow Republican, in the December 10 runoff by about 12 percentage points and took office January 3, 2017.

In the House he is a senior member of the Oversight and Government Reform Committee, where he chairs the Federal Law Enforcement Subcommittee, and he serves on the Armed Services Committee's Subcommittees on Seapower and Projection Forces and on Readiness.
His official biography says the Center for Effective Lawmaking ranked him among the most effective Republican legislators in the House.
He lives in Lafayette with his wife, Becca.
